DEV-66.description:
## The problem

Two of DEV-62's defects have no contract text: the Conductor WAF blocked a dispatch message containing a `curl | tar` bootstrap line, and both `asciinema` and `script(1)` hung without a pty, so e2e evidence was a timestamped stdout log. Both need one sentence each so the next dispatch does not rediscover them.

## Goal

The README `## Ship-flow runtime` section states that dispatch messages carry no bootstrap or download line (the image preinstalls plugins and spacedock) and that a task body longer than the first message travels on a committed carrier the worker fetches by `git show`; and that CLI e2e evidence is a timestamped stdout log written by `scripts/ship-flow/e2e-cli.sh <sha> <flow.yaml>`, which runs each `Execute external` step at the pinned SHA and exits non-zero on the first failing step, seen to fail on a flow whose step exits 1.

## Non-goals

* Do not attempt to make asciinema work; recording is out of scope.
* Do not change e2e-pipeline; the script consumes its `Execute external` step shape only.
* Do not implement the preinstalled image.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-1 **`scripts/ship-flow/e2e-cli.sh` passes DEV-50's three-step CLI flow at `0144264343775f4c74f517ccea488a8ef91c44bc` and exits 1 on a flow with a `false` step; both logs recorded with timestamps.
* **AC-2** README states the no-bootstrap-line rule and the committed-carrier rule, naming the WAF block as the reason.
* **AC-3** The contract test reddens when either sentence is removed; the mutation runs are recorded.

## Route-back conditions

The accepted outcome or non-goals changed. Stop and return a structured planning delta that names the changed premise, affected acceptance evidence, and recommended change or stop.
DEV-66.title: Dispatch carrier and e2e evidence rules for cloud workers

DEV-65.description:
## The problem

DEV-62's worker reported `WITHOUT_IT_COMMAND: python3 .context/without-it-check.py`, a path to an untracked file the First Officer could not retrieve, so the First Officer wrote its own checker instead of running the worker's. The kernel's minimal-necessity clause requires a task-owned command; the ship-flow evidence contract does not yet say what shape that command must have.

## Goal

The README `## Ship-flow runtime` section defines the worker Evidence block, and in it `WITHOUT_IT_COMMAND` is one self-contained shell line that exits 0 on the candidate and non-zero after `WITHOUT_IT_REMOVED_VARIANT` is applied, references no file outside the candidate tree, and is run verbatim by the First Officer in a worktree with no secrets; `scripts/ship-flow/without-it.sh <sha> <command> <removed-variant>` runs both variants and exits 0 only when retained passes and removed fails, and it has been seen to exit non-zero on a command that passes both ways.

## Non-goals

* Do not add a generic without-it harness; the script only runs the two variants and compares exit codes.
* Do not change the kernel's minimal-necessity wording.
* Do not require a browser or recording.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-1 **`scripts/ship-flow/without-it.sh` exits 0 for DEV-50's candidate `0144264343775f4c74f517ccea488a8ef91c44bc` with a one-line command and the README-restore removed variant, and exits 1 for `true` as the command; both runs recorded.
* **AC-2** README defines the Evidence block fields `CANDIDATE_SHA`, `BRANCH`, `BASE_SHA`, `WITHOUT_IT_COMMAND`, `WITHOUT_IT_REMOVED_VARIANT`, and states the one-line, no-external-file, run-verbatim rule.
* **AC-3** The contract test reddens when the one-line rule sentence is removed; the mutation run is recorded.

## Route-back conditions

The accepted outcome or non-goals changed. Stop and return a structured planning delta that names the changed premise, affected acceptance evidence, and recommended change or stop.
DEV-65.title: WITHOUT_IT_COMMAND is one verbatim shell line the FO runs unchanged

DEV-64.description:
## The problem

During DEV-62 the First Officer polled the worker with `conductor session message --after <id>`; the CLI truncates the JSON at 64 KB and `--after` rejects sent-message ids, so the Evidence block was found only by `conductor sql` on `session_transcripts_view`. Nothing in the repository records this.

## Goal

The workflow README's ship-flow section (new, under a `## Ship-flow runtime` heading) states that worker transcripts are read through `conductor sql` against `session_transcripts_view`, names the two CLI failure modes, and ships one small script `scripts/ship-flow/worker-transcript.sh <session-id>` that prints the last fenced Evidence block or exits non-zero; the script has been seen to exit non-zero on a session with no Evidence block.

## Non-goals

* Do not change the Conductor CLI or file an upstream issue as part of this item.
* Do not add polling loops, daemons, or retry budgets; one read per invocation.
* Do not read or write Linear.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-1 **`scripts/ship-flow/worker-transcript.sh` prints the last `## Evidence` block for a session that has one, and exits 1 with `no evidence block` for a session that has none; both runs are recorded with the session ids.
* **AC-2** README `## Ship-flow runtime` names `conductor sql` as the read path and names the 64 KB truncation and `--after` rejection as the reasons.
* **AC-3** The contract test reddens when the README section is removed and passes when restored; the mutation run is recorded.

## Route-back conditions

The accepted outcome or non-goals changed. Stop and return a structured planning delta that names the changed premise, affected acceptance evidence, and recommended change or stop.
